reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 21. Nay or No: 19. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Democratic majority could be computed, 39 (98%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 207 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: Big game in Oregon today! Cheering on the Wolverines as they take on the Ducks. Go Blue!

Welcome to our new members of Michigan’s Congressional delegation! We are ready to get to work helping families across our state and building a stronger, more affordable Michigan. https://t.co/PT4gRBEowm

It's a new era for the Congressional Labor Caucus and the American worker.
 
Higher wages. Better working conditions. Protecting benefits and the right to organize. More good-paying union jobs. 
 
We've got a lot of work to do—but that's what the Labor Caucus and working men and women do best. So let's get it done.

On Veterans Day, we honor the sacrifices of those who have worn our nation’s uniform. This day means so much to me as I spend it with the brave men and women who have dedicated their lives to protecting us. We must ensure they receive the care and benefits they earned. https://t.co/ccK97qrD1e
People keep telling me to put down the juice and soda and drink some water. That’s fine but it better be sparkling with a hint of lime. https://t.co/uj7USyv6Qd
@riley_rogerson It was after a perforated ulcer. I gave my whole stockpile away. Unfortunate that willpower only lasted about six months.
Well, my doctor saw this. But I told her not to worry. These are the only DC’s I’ll never drink. https://t.co/lMXe73KLDh
Stunned to see my friend @RepAOC surprise me with a Diet Coke cake adorned with Michigan maize and blue! https://t.co/oCOnSA0mK9

Diet Coke always tastes better when you share it with a friend. 

Thank you for this “cake”, @RepAOC, I just hope my doctor doesn’t see this. https://t.co/up2eRxRZf6

Pete Hegseth is a danger to our national security and our brave servicemembers. 
 
It's time for him to go.

Are you a student interested in a career in political communications? The Office of Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is hiring a communications intern for the Spring 2027 semester in Washington, D.C.!
 
Learn more and apply here:
https://t.co/crbbbtnFk6 https://t.co/5lsByUOiUz

Want to use your photography skills for public service? The Office of Congresswoman Debbie Dingell is hiring a Michigan-based digital intern for the Spring 2027 semester!
 
Learn more and apply here:
https://t.co/crbbbtod9E https://t.co/grxppR5BDw

Americans didn’t vote for a party—they voted for change. 

Democrats are ready to get to work, and our top priority must be lowering everyday costs for working families. https://t.co/pdv4K2vgCN
Back to work. https://t.co/GDGSAhG2VS
We’re ready for rivalry week! Protecting the M is an important part of preparing for tonight, and these guys did a great job. Go Blue! https://t.co/QMkHvH1V6f

It wouldn’t be rivalry week without a little friendly competition. I’m confident the Wolverines will bring home the win for the fifth straight year. Care to make a bet, @GovWhitmer? Loser wears the other team’s colors for a day.

Congressional interns play a vital role in keeping our office running. Join our team and help serve communities across Southeast Michigan! 

Spring internship applications close on November 20. Learn more here:

See more here:
https://t.co/crbbbtnFk6
Apparently the lesson they took from Tuesday was that Stephen Miller needed more responsibility. https://t.co/zp4D1yS2Oc

Winning an election is only the beginning. 

What matters now is what we do with the opportunity and the trust people have placed in us.

The American people want results. We are ready to get to work. Let’s get it done.

Our priorities must be clear: lower costs, make affordable healthcare accessible to all, end endless wars, and hold accountable those who put their own power and special interests ahead of working families.

People are working harder than ever and still struggling to afford a dignified life. They deserve a government that works hard for them.

The American people have entrusted Democrats with a majority in Congress. 

That trust comes with a responsibility — and an obligation to deliver.

My doctor sent me a note last night about my Diet Coke consumption (I didn’t know she followed me).

Thought I’d better start with orange juice this morning instead. https://t.co/zDWDkxo4pp
I’m on my 30th Diet Coke of the day. My good friend @GovWhitmer is going with something a little stronger. https://t.co/SWQ6DEq4qj
Fueling up for today! https://t.co/q93uQd43TH https://t.co/fnRzqBTvWn
There’s not enough Diet Coke in the world to make this Monday go by any faster.

Ann Arbor Fire Station #4 is now open—and it was named in honor of the city’s first woman firefighter, Mindy Kerr! Grateful for the work Mindy and all of Michigan’s firefighters do to keep our communities safe. https://t.co/GcRYeDpYPO
Reminder! The deadline to submit comments on the proposed framework for my Data Center Bill of Rights is this Friday, October 30. Please email your comments to DingellComments@mail.house.gov.
Ran into David Hogg at the UM tailgates. Always great to cheer on the Wolverines with people working to make a difference. Go Blue! https://t.co/9lqGvPXGfP
It’s game day! Excited to watch the Wolverines take on the reigning national champion, Indiana. Today also marks a historic milestone: Michigan’s 800th game as a Big Ten member. Go Blue!

My Ann Arbor office received a suspicious letter yesterday, consistent with reports from other congressional offices. Because we knew what to expect, it was not opened in our office, and local law enforcement and the FBI are handling. 

Threats like this are unacceptable. My offices are open, and no one should let the senders of these letters intimidate us.

Today’s ICE enforcement activity in Canton near a school resulted in a school lockdown and understandably caused fear and concern throughout the community. The local police department was not notified in advance.
 
I have been in contact with ICE, which acknowledged that there were issues with today’s enforcement activities. I will continue working with ICE, the township supervisor, and other relevant parties to address these concerns.
It’s homecoming at UM! Cheering on the Wolverines as they play Penn State here in Ann Arbor. Go Blue!

Stopped by Alpha House’s 31st Annual Gimmie Shelter. Everyone deserves a safe, permanent place to call home, and I will continue working to expand families’ access to the support and resources they need. https://t.co/WERoKzCCmr

My thoughts and prayers are with Congressman Krishnamoorthi, the people of Aurora, and Hindu and Indian American communities across the country in the wake of this horrific attempted attack. 

No one should have to fear for their safety because of their faith. This hate has no place in America, and we all must stand up to it whenever and wherever we see it.

Always enjoy spending time with students at the University Michigan. 

With these young leaders ready to make their mark, I am confident Michigan’s future will be bright. https://t.co/lfpCQyQm86

66 years ago today, President Kennedy delivered a speech to students on the steps of the Michigan Union that would inspire the creation of the Peace Corps. Since then, thousands of homes have been built, children have been taught, and lives have been saved through their work.

Happy Indigenous Peoples’ Day! 

Today we celebrate the rich histories, cultures, and contributions of Indigenous communities across our country.

The president is continuing to abuse his power three weeks before an election. 

This is unprecedented, but unfortunately not surprising. Donald Trump has repeatedly targeted Congresswoman Omar with hateful rhetoric, contributing to death threats and violence. 

Political disagreements should never justify intimidation. No president should use the power of the federal government to threaten, silence, or intimidate political opponents.
https://t.co/zC3qRgDIKq

President Trump’s attempts to interfere with the Fed and fire Lisa Cook are nothing more than a political witch hunt. Lisa has been cleared of these baseless allegations, and this is yet another attempt by the president to push the limits of his power. Our economy needs steady stewardship, not politics.
https://t.co/jwT2EwZ6Xv
If a community chooses to build a data center, it should be the companies the bear the costs — not hardworking families. https://t.co/dG8Dmfuozq

People deserve to have their voices heard in any discussion on proposed data centers.

I am working on a data center Bill of Rights to ensure people have a seat at the table in the decision-making process and are not footing the check for any projects in their communities. https://t.co/sLy7kvG7UI

We need answers and accountability from United Airlines. 

No woman should have to put up with this — I don’t care if it’s on a plane, train, in the workplace, or anywhere else.
https://t.co/kg7BxSxYcb

President Trump is living in a bubble.

People have real concerns about what data centers could do to their communities. We need federal guardrails that make sure people are heard and they are not forced to foot the bill for these projects. https://t.co/WhmQypeo7t

I hear from Michiganders who are afraid about what data centers being developed in their communities will mean for them. 

That is why I am working on federal guardrails that ensure people have a seat at the table in the decision-making process.
https://t.co/tWoymWZMrO
Looking forward to a great game against Minnesota today in the 100th Little Brown Jug game. Let’s keep the trophy in Ann Arbor! Go Blue!

Innovation cannot come at the cost of people’s livelihoods and having their voices heard in the decision-making process.

That’s why I’m working on a federal framework for data centers that would establish guardrails for their development.
https://t.co/7XXh32JzZw

Chinese automakers sell vehicles worldwide at artificially low prices, relying on slave labor and subsidies.   Let’s call it what it is: a strategy to destroy America’s auto industry and the 10 million workers holding it up.
https://t.co/XpFtUpdg5Q

Michiganders are feeling the pressure of rising energy prices.  We need policies that lower costs for working men and women — not ones that hand Big Tech a blank check while 
asking Michiganders to pick up the tab.
https://t.co/rP1WDjTZrN

The rapid development of data centers has raised concerns across my district and the country. It is clear we need federal guardrails, and that's why I'm working on a federal data center ‘Bill of Rights’ that ensures communities have a seat at the table and their voices are heard.
 
Read more and share your thoughts here: https://t.co/kN9Yf1BUEH
We need policies that give consumers choices while ensuring the next generation of vehicles, including EVs, are developed and built right here in America.

We need stable policies that make transportation more affordable, support good-paying American jobs, and give our industry the certainty they need to invest, innovate, and compete. Michigan put the world on wheels, and I intend to make sure we remain competitive in the global marketplace.

The global auto industry is changing rapidly, and China and other countries are investing heavily in the technologies that will define the future. The global market wants electric vehicles, and we cannot afford to fall behind. Our auto industry cannot continue to be a political ping-pong ball every four years.

Americans should have the freedom to choose the vehicle that works best for them, whether that’s electric, hybrid, or an internal combustion engine. But consumer choice and American leadership are not mutually exclusive.

Today’s decision risks putting the American automotive industry at a competitive disadvantage while the rest of the world races ahead, and it also ignores the more pressing issue working men and women are facing right now with the cost-of-living crisis and the rising price of gas.
https://t.co/wG4qjd1Gjs

Just like democracy, pong is a team sport. And I pulled my weight for the team today.🍻

Always enjoy spending time with U-M students, especially on game day. GO BLUE! https://t.co/g1Ue6gu958
Another big game today as Michigan faces the Iowa Hawkeyes. And today is the annual beer pong game with College Dems. I know Michigan will win—we’ll see how I do. Go Blue!

A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
